items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the tax law, in relation to credits for premiums paid for long-term care insurance policies
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S2315

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the tax law, in relation to credits
for premiums paid for long-term care insurance policies

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

The purpose of this bill is to expand upon the provisions of Chapter
563 of the Laws of 2010 and Chapter 465 of the Laws of 2014, which
expanded the types of end of life care that can be financed by an
accelerated death benefit rider attached to a life insurance policy.
Under these new laws, persons who have resided in a nursing home for
three months or more or require end of life or palliative care for
three months or more at a residential,health care facility, receive
home care services or hospice care and such services are expected to
be needed until death can now be financed by a life insurance policy
rider. The bill provides additional tax credit inducements to
encourage individuals to purchase long term care insurance or these
new life insurance policy riders when they are younger.

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Amends Tax Law section 190 to increase the tax credit for
purchasing long term care insurance or a policy rider to a life
insurance policy that provides for long term care-like coverages. The
tax credit increases from 20% to 40% if the insured is less than 40
years old. The bill provides further a gradual decrease in the tax
credit based on age (but which is still higher than the current law
that establishes the tax credit at 20 percent). For persons less than
50 years old, the tax credit is 30%, for those older than 50, but less
than 55 years old, the tax credit is 25%, and for those 55 years old
or older, the tax credit remains the same as it is now at 20%.

The reason for the increase in the tax credit for those under the age
of 40, 50, and 55 years of age is to encourage younger persons to
purchase long term care insurance or policy riders to life insurance
policies when the premium rate is cheaper. Over 80% of the New York
Partnership for Long Term Care Insurance policies are purchased by
persons over the age of 55. For persons over the age of 60 years, the
average cost of a Partnership for Long Term Care insurance policy is
between $3,000 and $6,000, for those under the age of 55, it is
approximately $2,300. Hence, even with the higher percentage tax
credit for the purchase of LTC Insurance, for younger persons the tax
subsidy will be less than it is for the average person over the age of
60. The goal of this bill is to encourage younger individuals to
purchase this kind of coverage. For younger persons, the combination
of relatively low rates, plus the enhanced tax credit should help to
encourage more young people to purchase such long term care coverages.

Section 2: Amends Tax Law section 210-B to add the new tax credit
incentive for the computation of the corporate franchise tax.

Section 3: Amends Tax Law section 606 to add the long term care
insurance and LTC life insurance policy rider tax credit for personnel
income tax calculations.


Section 4: Amends Tax Law section 1511 to add the LTC tax credit for
insurance corporation taxes.

JUSTIFICATION:

As the general population becomes older, more and more individuals are
looking for affordable ways to finance their nursing home and long
term care needs. While there are available policies that provide
payment for long term care, more products should be authorized under
New York law so that consumers will have more types of insurance
coverage available to meet their specific needs or the needs of their
family.

In addition, encouraging more individuals to finance their own long
term care, will help to curtail future expenditures from the State's
Medicaid program, which currently finances the lion's share of the
provision of long term care in this State. This bill is a further
extension of new laws such as Chapter 563 of the Laws of 2010 and
Chapter 465 of the Laws of 2014 which are geared towards encouraging
individuals to finance their own long term care and nursing home care
as we all get older via life insurance policy riders.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2011-2012 - S. 5037 - Referred to Insurance;
2013-2014 - Referred to Insurance Committee

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

It is the intent of this bill encourage the increased us: of Long Term
Care insurance and policy riders to life insurance policies for the
use as a financing mechanism to finance end of life care. This, in the
end, should help to decrease State Medicaid expenditures.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect on April, 1st of the year next succeeding
its date of enactment.

A.actClause: AN ACT to amend the tax law and the insurance law, in relation to credits for premiums paid for long-term care insurance policies
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S2315A

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the tax law and the insurance law, in relation to
credits for premiums paid for long-term care insurance policies

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

The purpose of this bill is to expand upon the provisions of Chapter
563 of the Laws of 2010 and Chapter 465 of the Laws of 2014, which
expanded the types of end of life care that can be financed by an
accelerated death benefit rider attached to a life insurance policy.
Under these new laws, persons who have resided in a nursing home for
three months or more or require end of life or palliative care for
three months or more at a residential, health care facility, receive
home care services or hospice care and such services are expected to
be needed until death can now be financed by a life insurance policy
rider. The bill provides additional tax credit inducements to
encourage individuals to purchase long term care insurance or these
new life insurance policy riders when they are younger.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Sections 1 - 4: Amends Tax Law sections 190, 210-B, 606, and 1511 to
increase the tax credit for purchasing long term care insurance or a
policy rider to a life insurance policy that provides for long term
care-like coverages. The tax credit increases from 20% to 40% if the
insured is less than 40 years old. The bill provides further a gradual
decrease in the tax credit based on age (but which is still higher
than the current law that establishes the tax credit at 20 percent).
For persons less than 50 years old, the tax credit is 30%, for those
older than 50, but less than 55 years old, the tax credit is 25%, and
for those 55 years old or older, the tax credit remains the same as it
is now at 20%.

Section 5: Amends Insurance Law section 1117 to make technical
reference changes to ensure that the Department of Financial Services
can review and approve of such Life Insurance Policy riders that cover
Long Term Care services and ensure that they qualify for the Long Term
Care tax credit.

 JUSTIFICATION :

The reason for the increase in the tax credit for those under the age
of 40, 50, and 55 years of age is to encourage younger persons to
purchase long term care insurance or policy riders to life insurance
policies when the premium rate is cheaper. Over 80% of the New York
Partnership for Long Term Care Insurance policies are purchased by
persons over the age of 55. For persons over the age of 60 years, the
average cost of a Partnership for Long Term Care insurance policy is
between $3,000 and $6,000, for those under the age of 55, it is
approximately $2,300.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on April, 1st of the year next succeeding
its date of enactment.

summary: Establishes tax credits for premiums paid for life insurance which is used for long term health care; enhances tax credits for long term health care insurance premiums.
